affected_party: QIF evaluators, policy owners, and stakeholders protected by loss boundaries
actual_problem: QIF records reviewed rubric revisions and route-policy snapshots, but cannot replay the same preserved decision evidence against a candidate route policy before authorization to reveal route changes and hypothetical loss-boundary tradeoffs.
why_it_matters: A policy owner may approve a plausible change without seeing which prior decisions would route differently or which protected outcomes could be exposed, while a naive replay could falsely imply optimality or authority.
why_now: v0.6.39 established governed revision candidates and replay scope; current counterfactual-evaluation practice emphasizes same-input experiments, explicit labels, blind evidence, and trace-level comparison.
